controls.name: Check for updates
controls.tip: Ask GitHub about every product now. It only reads public release data; nothing is sent about you or this computer.
controls.default: Also runs once when the app opens

controls.name: Settings
controls.tip: Look, hover bubbles, install mode and the optional GitHub sign in.

controls.name: About
controls.tip: What this is, what it collects (nothing), and how to remove it.

controls.name: Updates tab
controls.tip: Products that have a newer version than the one installed.

controls.name: All tab
controls.tip: Every public Studio 87 product. Updates come first.

controls.name: VST and FX tab
controls.tip: VST3 effects, analysers, editors and tools.

controls.name: Synths tab
controls.tip: Synths and instruments.

controls.name: Controllers tab
controls.tip: Plugins that control a hardware synth or effect unit.

controls.name: Apps and logue tab
controls.tip: Standalone apps and logue units (minilogue xd, drumlogue).

controls.name: Installed tab
controls.tip: Products found on this computer.

controls.name: Not installed tab
controls.tip: Products not installed yet. Pick Install on a row.

controls.name: Search box
controls.tip: Type to filter the list by name, kind (for example controller) or status (for example update).

controls.name: Update / Install selected
controls.tip: Update or install the products you ticked, one after another.

controls.name: Update all / Install all
controls.tip: Update every product that has a newer version. Products with an unknown installed version are left alone.
controls.range: Click (acts on the tab you see)

controls.name: Row tick box
controls.tip: Tick to include this product in the batch button above the list.

controls.name: Update / Install button
controls.tip: Download, verify the SHA256 checksums, then install 0.2.4. Installers are not code-signed: Windows or macOS may show a warning. Nothing is installed until you click.

controls.name: Changelog button
controls.tip: Read the release notes for every version newer than the one you have.

controls.name: GitHub button
controls.tip: Open the project page in your browser.

controls.name: Roll back button
controls.tip: Put back the version that was installed before the last update: version 0.2.2. The newer one is removed.
controls.range: Click; only shown when a previous version is kept

controls.name: Smaller window
controls.tip: Smaller. Drag a corner to scale everything; drag a side to change only the width or the height.

controls.name: Fit to screen
controls.tip: Back to the normal size for this screen. Double click on either wood side does the same.

controls.name: One to one
controls.tip: Show everything at its design size (1:1).

controls.name: Larger window
controls.tip: Bigger.

displays.name: Screenshot
displays.text: The product's own docs/screenshot.png at 310 x 162, taken from the catalog's small thumbnail (or from the repository when the catalog has none), fetched during the check and saved on disk. Products without one show a tinted 'no screenshot yet' tile.

displays.name: Name, kind and build type
displays.text: Product name, its kind (VST3 plugin, standalone app, hardware controller, logue unit) and TEST BUILD when the release is marked as a pre-release or called a test build.

displays.name: Installed and latest version
displays.text: What is really installed (read from the plugin's own metadata, the system's installer records or what this updater installed) and the newest release on GitHub. 'unknown' and 'not installed' are shown honestly.

displays.name: Status
displays.text: Update available, Up to date, Not installed, Installed version unknown, No release yet, Could not check, or View on GitHub. While working it turns into the stage (Downloading, Verifying SHA256, Installing) with a progress bar. After an update or a Roll back it shows the result message of that row.

displays.name: Description
displays.text: The start of the release notes, wrapped to two lines. The Changelog button shows the notes of every version newer than yours.

displays.name: Date, size and install route
displays.text: Release date, download size and how this product gets installed on this system. 'saved list' means the answer came from disk (offline or rate limited).

displays.name: Status line
displays.text: The result of the last action (for example '3 of 4 done.' or a Roll back message). The small line under it says when the catalog was read and turns amber when the catalog is more than 9 hours old. 'N of M shown' is on the right; a GitHub rate-limit or offline message appears in red on the right.

displays.name: Scrolling list
displays.text: One long list of the tab you are on. Use the mouse wheel, drag, or the arrow keys; there are no scrollbars. In the All tab products with an update come first.

displays.name: Size read-out
displays.text: Design size in pixels and the zoom percent. Drag a corner to scale everything; drag a side to change only the width (960 to 1500) or the height (760 to 1500).

displays.name: Wood sides
displays.text: Double click on either wood side to go back to the normal size for this screen.

controls.name: Stop after this one
controls.tip: Finish the current product, then stop the rest.

controls.name: Update all / Install all (waiting)
controls.tip: Update every product that has a newer version. Products with an unknown installed version are left alone.

controls.name: Row progress (status area of the row)
controls.tip: While a product is installing, its status line shows the stage (Downloading, Verifying SHA256, Installing) and a bar. A row's buttons stay off until it is done.

controls.name: Update the updater
controls.tip: Download the newer Studio 87 Gear Updater, check its SHA256, then hand over to its installer. Nothing is replaced until the check passes; the old version keeps working if anything fails.
controls.default: Hidden unless a newer release exists

controls.name: Check for updates (leaves offline mode)
controls.tip: Ask GitHub about every product now. It only reads public release data; nothing is sent about you or this computer.

displays.name: Update the updater first bar
displays.text: Appears under the tabs when a newer Studio 87 Gear Updater release exists. The button hands over to the new installer after its SHA256 check passes. While it works, the bar shows 'Updating the updater: downloading N%'. The version in this picture (v0.1.3) is an example.

displays.name: Offline bar
displays.text: Appears when GitHub could not be reached: 'Offline, showing saved list from <date and time of the saved copy>'. Install and Update are off with a reason, unless the installer was already downloaded. The date in this picture is an example.

controls.name: Page up
controls.tip: Show the previous page of the release notes. There are no scrollbars.

controls.name: Page down
controls.tip: Show the next page of the release notes. There are no scrollbars.

controls.name: Refresh now
controls.tip: Ask GitHub directly about this product, for the newest answer right now. Uses 1 of the 60 free requests per hour.

controls.name: Open on GitHub
controls.tip: Open this release on GitHub in your browser.

controls.name: Close
controls.tip: Close this window. Nothing is changed.

displays.name: Installed and latest
displays.text: The installed version (or 'unknown') and the newest release on GitHub.

displays.name: Release notes
displays.text: The notes of every release newer than the installed one, newest first, as written on GitHub (the newest one only when the installed version is unknown). Page up and Page down move through it; there are no scrollbars.

controls.name: Cancel
controls.tip: Go back. Nothing is downloaded or installed.

controls.name: Update 3
controls.tip: Start now: each product is downloaded, its SHA256 checked, then installed, one after another. One failure does not stop the others.

displays.name: What will happen
displays.text: Says that each product is downloaded, its SHA256 checked, then installed, and that a mismatch stops that product only.

displays.name: Products and warning
displays.text: The products and versions in this batch (the first 12, then 'and N more'), and the note that the installers are not code-signed and that presets are never touched.

controls.name: Retry failed
controls.tip: Run only the products that did not finish again. A download that was cut off continues where it stopped.
controls.range: Click; shows the number to retry

controls.name: Close
controls.tip: Close this window. Nothing is changed.

displays.name: Summary
displays.text: How many products finished and how many did not. A failure never stops the others.

displays.name: One entry per product
displays.text: Done (green), Failed or Stopped (red), the product name and the message: what was installed, or why it was refused. The entries in this picture are examples, written for this manual.

controls.name: Look: Neon Navy
controls.tip: Switch the whole window to this colour look now. Saved on this computer; the wood sides, cat logo and layout stay the same.

controls.name: Look: Purple Soda Pop
controls.tip: Switch the whole window to this colour look now. Saved on this computer; the wood sides, cat logo and layout stay the same.

controls.name: Look: PurrOne
controls.tip: Switch the whole window to this colour look now. Saved on this computer; the wood sides, cat logo and layout stay the same.

controls.name: Hover bubbles: On or Off
controls.tip: Switch the info bubbles that appear after about one second of hovering on or off.

controls.name: GitHub account: Sign in with GitHub / Sign out
controls.tip: Optional. Raises GitHub's hourly limit from 60 to 5000 requests. No permissions are requested.

controls.name: Keep sign in: Keychain or file
controls.tip: The token goes into the system keychain; if there is none (Flatpak, headless) into an encrypted file in the app data folder that only you can read (casual protection only).
controls.range: Keychain or file; This session only

controls.name: Keep sign in: This session only
controls.tip: The token is kept in memory only and is gone when you close the app.
controls.range: Keychain or file; This session only

controls.name: Install mode: No admin needed on Linux
controls.tip: On Linux plugins go to ~/.vst3 or a user-level Flatpak, so there is nothing to choose and no password prompt.
controls.range: Linux has no choice (Windows and macOS: All users or Just for me)
controls.default: Just for me (Linux); All users (Windows, macOS)

controls.name: Linux plugins go to: Automatic
controls.tip: Use the Flatpak extension when that product's extension is already installed, otherwise put the plugin in ~/.vst3.

controls.name: Linux plugins go to: VST3 folder
controls.tip: Always put the plugin in ~/.vst3 (for DAWs that are not Flatpaks).

controls.name: Linux plugins go to: Flatpak DAW
controls.tip: Always install the Flatpak extension (for Flatpak DAWs). The DAW must use the same Freedesktop runtime.

controls.name: Saved list: Clear (size)
controls.tip: Delete the saved catalog, release info and screenshots used for offline mode. Plugins and settings are not touched. The next check downloads them again.
controls.range: Click; the saved list is capped at 60 MB

controls.name: Previous versions: Clear (size)
controls.tip: Delete the previous plugin versions kept for Roll back. Installed plugins are not touched.
controls.range: Click; previous versions are capped at 600 MB

controls.name: Close
controls.tip: Close this window. Nothing is changed.

displays.name: Sign in status
displays.text: Says whether you are signed in and where the token is kept: OS keychain, local file or this session only. After an expired sign in it says 'Your GitHub sign in expired. Please sign in again'.

displays.name: Saved list note
displays.text: What offline mode keeps (the list, product info and screenshots, never plugin files) and the size cap.

displays.name: Previous versions note
displays.text: What Roll back keeps (the last version before each update, plugin folders only) and the size cap.

displays.name: Install mode explanation
displays.text: What the install mode means on this system. On Linux it also says what Automatic does and that presets are never touched.

controls.name: Cancel
controls.tip: Stop signing in. Nothing is stored.

displays.name: Reminder
displays.text: Sign in is optional and requests no permissions.

displays.name: Code to type
displays.text: The web address and the one-time code to type there. The app opens the address in your browser by itself and waits until you approve. In this picture the code is an example from a stub, not a real GitHub code.

controls.name: Ko-fi (optional tip)
controls.tip: Optional. Opens the Studio 87 Ko-fi page in your browser when you click. Nothing is locked behind it and the app never asks again.

controls.name: GitHub
controls.tip: Open the source code and the releases of this updater on GitHub.

controls.name: Close
controls.tip: Close this window. Nothing is changed.

displays.name: Version and licence
displays.text: The version of this updater and its licence.

displays.name: What it is and what it stores
displays.text: What the app does, that it collects nothing, the folder where it keeps its own files (on this computer), how Roll back works, the unsigned-installer note and how to remove it.

controls.name: Open Settings
controls.tip: Open Settings to change the install mode, the look and the hover bubbles.

controls.name: Got it
controls.tip: Close this welcome note. It is only shown once.

displays.name: Install mode
displays.text: The install mode in force on this system.

displays.name: How installing works here
displays.text: One short explanation of when an administrator prompt can appear (Windows and macOS, All users only) or that none is ever needed (Linux). Shown once, the first time the app is opened.

signed_in: Signed in, token stored in: OS keychain
Signed in, token stored in: local file
Signed in, token stored in: this session only
status_lines.expired: Your GitHub sign in expired. Please sign in again (the list works without it).
status_lines.out: Not signed in (optional). A new sign in would be kept in: <where it would go>
